analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Vopak is a capital-heavy LPG/chemical terminalling infrastructure play with strong top-line growth (revenue 353→621 Cr in 2 years) but weak ROE of 8.73% and ROCE of 7.01% — this is not the innovation-led, high-return compounder my framework seeks. At 109x trailing P/E and 31x sales, the market already prices in decades of flawless execution for a business with no R&D moat.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR ~33% FY23-FY25 with operating margins near 48%, reflecting pricing power in scarce terminal capacity
Royal Vopak partnership brings global terminalling expertise and disciplined operating standards
Tangible infrastructure assets (tanks, jetties) create high barriers to entry in coastal LPG/liquid storage
key_risks: ROE 8.73% and ROCE 7.01% are well below my 20%+ threshold despite fat EBITDA margins — capital intensity destroys returns
Valuation extreme: 109x P/E, 31x P/S, 55x EV/EBITDA for an infra asset, not a tech innovator
Finance cost 193 Cr consumes ~60% of operating income; any rate shock or capex overrun hits net profit of just 127 Cr hard
red_flags: Zero R&D intensity — this is a tollbooth, not an innovation compounder I would own
Net profit of 127 Cr on 7,072 Cr assets = 1.8% ROA, a structurally low-quality return profile
Persistent negative FCF until FY25 (2022: -64, 2023: -6, 2024: -325); single year of positive FCF (350 Cr) is not a track record
analysis.detailed_analysis: From my framework, this fails at the first question: does the company have products with years of sales growth AND the return profile to compound capital at high rates? Terminalling is a capacity-constrained tollbooth business — growth comes from building new tanks, which requires enormous capex (investing CF of -1,786, -857, -378 Cr over three years) financed by equity dilution and debt. The 48% operating margin looks seductive until you see ROCE collapse to 7% because the denominator (7,072 Cr of assets) is enormous. There is no R&D, no innovation flywheel, no scuttlebutt-worthy product excellence — just steel tanks leased to oil majors.\n\nManagement (via the Vopak JV) is competent and disciplined, and the 86.94% promoter holding shows alignment, but even excellent operators cannot turn an infrastructure utility into a 20%+ ROE compounder. At 42x forward P/E the market is extrapolating the capacity-expansion pipeline as if it were a SaaS business; if utilization or tariffs disappoint, the re-rating downside is severe. I would prefer to own Aegis Logistics directly, or better yet, a genuine innovator with expanding margins and R&D optionality. Pass — interesting business, wrong price, wrong return profile for my style.
